items.name: Coordinate frame of all positions
items.value: ltp-nad83-2011 (tools/geo_frame.py): x east, z south, metres from the FAA ARP; heights in metres above the local apron unless stated

items.name: What the SFO Museum boarding-area polygons are
items.value: departure-level (sfo:level 2) floor outlines, not roof outlines; roof edges measured on NAIP lie 0-5 m outside them on the ESE (airfield) faces and 0-2 m inside on the WNW faces (see *.roof_edges)

items.name: Sun / shadow vector on NAIP 2020 over the domestic terminals
items.method: ATCT shadow azimuth on NAIP 2020 (87.4 +- 1.5 deg), elevation fixed on the 2020-05-24 sun path (NOAA algorithm, dom_sun.py) and scaled so that FAA DOF 06-035331 (BA F arm roof, 34 ft) and Boarding Area A (k from DOF poles) are reproduced; implied time ~16:45 PDT

items.name: Sun / shadow vector on NAIP 2024
items.method: FAA DOF pole 06-034826 (108 ft) shadow (ITB research); on the 2024-05-20 sun path at 13:14 PDT (dom_sun.py)

items.name: Control 1: Boarding Area A main-body roof (ITB pier) by the two-epoch method
items.note: lean solved k24.x = 0.418 vs 0.413 from the FAA DOF poles (ITB research, extrapolated 116 m): agreement 1 %; the ITB research gives 17.0 m (low confidence) with its own single-epoch band

items.name: Control 2: Boarding Area F north-east arm roof vs FAA DOF 06-035331
items.note: DOF 34 ft AGL / 44 ft AMSL, 1A, surveyed 2013 (JDATE 2013289) at world (-1027.2, -211.2): roof of the arm, west edge. Difference +0.67 m = 1.0 sigma of the measurement + DOF vertical tolerance

items.name: Name / composition
items.value: Harvey Milk Terminal 1 (formerly South Terminal, 1963): Boarding Area B (gates B2-B27), Terminal 1 Center (check-in, security, baggage claim) and Boarding Area C (C1-C11)

items.name: Opening phases of the redevelopment
items.value: BA-B first 9 gates + checkpoint + part of T1 Center: July 2019 (23 Jul 2019); 9 more gates + south check-in lobby: May 2020; BA-B complete 2021; final phase (north check-in lobby, mezzanine checkpoint, gates B3 and C1, connector linking all terminals post-security): 17 Jun 2024

items.name: Design / build teams
items.value: BA-B: design-builder Austin Commercial + Webcor Builders JV, architects HKS / Woods Bagot / ED2 International / KYA JV (+ Tsao Design Group), engineer Arup; T1 Center: design-builder Hensel Phelps, architects Gensler / Kuth Ranieri JV; construction manager AECOM / Cooper Pugeda JV (T1C), WSP / Parsons Brinckerhoff / AGS (BA-B)

items.name: Floor areas (published, differing definitions)
items.note: BA-B: 619,150 sf (DBIA, Southland, RDH ~619,000), 617,700 sf "on 3 levels" (Airport Improvement 2020), 46,000 m2 / 500,000 sf (Woods Bagot); T1 Center: 1.1 million sf (Kuth Ranieri), 900,000 SF (Hensel Phelps)

items.name: Aircraft gates
items.note: incl. 4 international swing gates (Airport Improvement); Webcor: "24 new gates"; Wikipedia counts 26 (B2-B27) after B3 opened in 2024

items.name: Levels
items.value: apron level + concourse (departure) level + mezzanine (airline clubs, international corridor): "two levels and a mezzanine" (Arup) = "three-story" (RDH) = "3 levels" (Airport Improvement)

items.name: Structure
items.value: Type I cast-in-place concrete frame on a pile foundation; piles 100 ft deep (seismic)

items.name: Facade glazing
items.value: electrochromic (View Dynamic Glass) glazing throughout the concourse level, 112,000 sq ft; Low-E high-performance glazing at the clerestory level; floor-to-ceiling windows at the gates

items.name: Roof section: raised concourse with clerestory
items.value: central concourse ceiling rises to a clerestory band glazed on both sides (interior photos 2019-2024 and Arup "clerestory level"); gate holdrooms along the airfield faces
items.note: geometry (clerestory height and width) not published; visible in Commons photo p02 (Elbeaux 2024) and the Woods Bagot interior photos (reference only)

items.name: Rooftop photovoltaic array
items.note: "1 MW solar array located on the building's roof" (Arup, RDH, HKS extract); "1.2-MWDC rooftop array consisting of nearly 3,000 photovoltaic (PV) panels" (Cupertino Electric)

items.name: PV layout on the roof (imaged)
items.value: rows parallel to the pier axis, each ~5.5 m wide at ~9 m pitch, covering the concourse roof between the airfield edge and the central clerestory/skylight strip; a narrow row along the ESE (airfield) roof edge
items.method: NAIP 2020/2024 cross-profiles (dom_profile.py) and the Google screenshot b1d51b0f (reference only)

items.name: Roof wells / courtyards on the landside (WNW) part
items.value: the Civic Design Review Committee asked the team to investigate "the use of roof wells as intake zones" (Aug 2016); imagery shows long sunken roof courtyards with planting on the WNW side of the pier (north half) crossed by two bridges

items.name: Outer roof edge height above apron, south half (t -1238..-1176)
items.method: h = (band20 + band24 - p) / ((s20 - s24) . n) (dom_heights.py; |s20| calibrated 1.19 +- 0.03)
items.note: the dark ESE perimeter strip (6 m) and the PV field shift alike between epochs (3.3 / 3.4 m), i.e. same height within +-1.5 m; the central clerestory rises above this (not measured)

items.name: Lean-free roof edges, south half (world lines)
items.note: ESE roof edge 3.3 m outside the SFO Museum level-2 outline (roof overhang), WNW edge 1.6 m inside it; roof width 55.4 m vs outline 53.7 m (+-1 m)

items.name: Exterior metal / glass palette
items.value: glass and painted metal panels (airside); the team proposed metal spandrel panels instead of continuous louvres for exhaust/intake (CDR Phase 2, Aug 2016)
items.note: colours not published; T3W CDR cites "electrochromic glass (Terminal 1)" as a campus cue

items.name: Height of the skylight trusses above the Main Hall (Level 3) floor
items.note: "inserted within the truss structure of the skylights, 70 feet above the floor" - floor = Main Hall, Level 3, pre-security; the floor elevation above the apron is not published

items.name: Skylight light reflectors (art, James Carpenter)
items.note: each reflector sits in a skylight -> at least four skylights >= 55 m x 9 m; AIP 2020 (phase 1) mentions "three large skylights"

items.name: Number of main-hall skylights
items.note: 3 in the 2020 article (only half the hall existed then); 4 reflectors in the finished hall. Not identified on NAIP 2024 (roof is saturated white with PV)

items.name: Landside (curb) facade
items.value: two-tier fritted-glass curtain wall with vertical mullions (pattern "reminiscent of Redwood trees") above a continuous glass canopy over the departures curb; clear glass below the canopy; warm (wood) entries
items.note: CDR Aug 2016: "fritted glass ... the top half material of the landside of the terminal, while the glass below the canopy would remain clear"; laminated-wood vestibules; photos: Commons p00 (Famartin 2025-08-12), RDH facade photos (reference only)

items.name: Main-hall roof
items.value: roof almost entirely covered by PV rows laid out radially (fan) following the curved hall; three ~9 x 11 m light-blue glazed openings visible at world (-826, 460), (-815, 508), (-884, 530)
items.method: visual reading of NAIP 2024 at 0.2 m/px (t1hall_2024_z.jpg); positions +-3 m, lean-affected

items.name: Main-hall roof height above apron
items.note: not measured: curved faces, the landside faces are over roadways/garage and the airfield face has a strip whose shadow is ambiguous; lower bound ~ Level 3 floor + 70 ft (21.3 m)

items.name: FAA DOF building points on the old (pre-2019) Terminal 1
items.note: surveyed 2013 (JDATE 2013289): 06-035351 50 ft at (-881.4, 518.1) was on the old T1 center (demolished 2019-2023); 06-035323 17 ft at (-696.7, 628.7) and 06-035322 24 ft at (-620.2, 493.1) are on the apron today (old structures or jet bridges). Superseded - do not use for the new T1

items.name: Gates
items.note: gate C1 opened 17 Jun 2024 (SFO); total from Wikipedia

items.name: History
items.value: pier of the 1963 South Terminal (Welton Becket and Associates), renovated 1988 and "refreshed" with the T1 Center project (2024); between Jun 2020 and Oct 2024 counted as part of Terminal 2

items.name: Roof edge height above apron, east half, NNE face (single-face estimate)
items.method: h = (band20 + band24 - p) / ((s20 - s24) . n) (dom_heights.py; |s20| calibrated 1.19 +- 0.03)
items.note: single-face method with an assumed lean k24.x = 0.40 +- 0.06 (from the two-epoch sites); the west half gives an inconsistent band (neighbouring T1 structures in the 2020 shadow)

items.name: Roof features (imaged)
items.value: two long dark bands along the pier on both sides of a lighter central spine (glazed roof monitors or dark roofing - unresolved), a light-blue glazed patch near world (-675, 415) on NAIP 2024, rounded ESE end

items.name: History
items.value: opened 27 Aug 1954 as the Central Terminal; rebuilt as the International Terminal (Gensler, 1983); closed 2000; renovated and reopened 14 Apr 2011 (Gensler with Turner, design-build, $383 M) with 14 gates

items.name: Area / levels
items.value: 640,000 sq ft, two-level structure

items.name: Daylighting
items.value: custom clerestory windows and skylights over the ticketing lobby and recompose areas; transparent (west-facing) facade; interior "floating angular planes" (clouds) below the roof
items.note: positions/sizes of the clerestories and skylights are not published

items.name: Photovoltaics
items.value: 456-kW PV system on an adjacent SFO building (not on T2) providing ~20 % of T2 power

items.name: Former ATCT on Terminal 2
items.value: the pre-2016 control tower stood on top of T2 (photos 2009, 2013); replaced by the 2016 ATCT; its removal date is covered by the tower research

items.name: Landside facade
items.value: light metal-panel box with the "Terminal 2" sign and a glass entry wall ("neutral exterior, warm interior"; "massing hierarchy") - T3W CDR campus study

items.name: Roof height above apron, D head (ESE face) paired with the south WNW face 90 m away
items.method: h = (band20 + band24 - p) / ((s20 - s24) . n) (dom_heights.py; |s20| calibrated 1.19 +- 0.03)
items.note: two-epoch method, but the two faces may belong to different roof levels; FAA DOF (2013) gives 25 ft (7.6 m) at (-486.9, 71.9) and 24 ft (7.3 m) at (-482.1, 257.8) near the head corners (+-6 m horizontal)

items.name: FAA DOF building points at the D head
items.note: 06-035330 (-486.9, 71.9), 06-035321 (-482.1, 257.8), 06-035320 (-444.3, 194.0; 30 m east of the head, probably a jet bridge / apron structure). 2013 survey, T2 unchanged since 2011

items.name: Roof features (imaged)
items.value: large trapezoidal head with two semicircular (horseshoe) roof features at its NW and SE ends and linear skylights; pier from T2 heading ESE

items.name: History
items.value: North Terminal by San Francisco Airport Architects (John Carl Warnecke and Associates, Dreyfuss + Blackford, minority architects): groundbreaking 22 Apr 1971, BA F opened 1979, BA E 1981; BA-E renovated 2014 and T3 East rebuilt (Hensel Phelps / Gensler; Wikipedia: 2015); T3 West modernisation under construction since Aug 2024 (completion expected 2029)
items.note: original architects and dates only via Wikipedia

items.name: Project floor elevations (95% CD, Oct 2023)
items.note: sheet 5A-A5.01.01/.02 level markers; datum not stated on the sheets (see t3.heights_above_L1)

items.name: Heights above the T3 arrivals floor (L1)
items.method: elevation minus L1 TOC (11'-0" T3, 10'-3" T3W)
items.note: apron vs L1: DOF ground near T3 is 9-10 ft AMSL (06-035331: 44-34; 06-035332: 25-16); if the project datum is ~AMSL, L1 is 1-2 ft above the apron [inf, unverified]

items.name: Airside "field" facade wall section (new, under construction)

value.window_heights: 10'-0" x2 with a 2'-0" horizontal mullion band

items.note: CDR p.18; materials: ACM panel, aluminium window wall with vertical fins, accent frame / deluge concealment, single-ply roofing

items.name: Airside "gatehouse" facade wall section (new F1-F4 gatehouses)
items.note: CDR p.20; roof = mechanical penthouse; escalator/stair behind glazing

items.name: New T3W exterior material legend (95% CD)
items.value: ACM rainscreen panels "Duranar XL Whetstone Gray Metallic" (MP-50), "Duranar Sunstorm Norfolk Gray Mica" dark gray (MP-51), "Focus Black" (MP-52); perforated metal panel to match the existing T3E penthouse; electrochromic glazing (GL-50); insulated glass with frit (GL-51); laminated insulated skylight glazing (GL-60); aluminium window wall and vertical mullion fins (dark gray metallic)

items.name: Post-Phase-3 change (May 2026)
items.value: SFO and United agreed to enlarge the lounge: one additional storey on the airside / east side; Level 2M/3 club 22,950 SF, Level 4 club 22,450 SF, Level 5 mechanical penthouse 15,300 SF
items.note: the as-built T3W massing is therefore not final; model the 2024 (pre-construction) state or the approved design only after the owner decides

items.name: T3W project scope
items.value: renovate the existing 650,000 sq ft western half of T3 (seismic retrofit, security, check-in), +200,000 sq ft new; new six-storey Courtyard 4 (C4C) building; FIS sterile connector to the ITB; complete replacement of the T3 facade; $2.6 B

items.name: T3 East exterior (existing, reference for T3W)
items.value: clear perimeter glass with grey frit, metal panel (platinum), metal panel (dark gray metallic), aluminium vertical mullion fins, metal brow surround; rooftop mechanical penthouse clad in perforated/corrugated light-gray metal with wide-profile corrugated accent stripes
items.note: CDR p.8 and p.16 photos (reference only)

items.name: T3 East size
items.note: Studio 151: 400,000 SF renovation + 53,000 SF expansion adding 3 gates; MKA: 320,000 ft2, three-story

items.name: Existing rooftop mechanical penthouses
items.value: one large penthouse on T3 East and a row of smaller penthouses on T3 West (CDR "Existing Massing"); new T3W penthouses added by the project
items.note: plan sizes and heights not dimensioned in the CDR set

items.name: BA-E renovation
items.value: design-build Hensel Phelps with Gensler and the KPA Group; unveiled 25 Jan 2014; $138 M; 10 United gates; complete demolition from the concourse level up and a 30,000 SF concourse expansion; LEED Gold; part of the T3 East capital program (68,800 sf BA-E + 150,000 sf eastern concourse)

items.name: BA-E roof
items.value: "With tapered edges overhanging clerestory glazing, the roof is structured with lightweight, long-span trusses concealed within a finished architectural ceiling" (middle two column rows removed)

items.name: BA-E facade
items.value: clear perimeter glass (with grey frit where fritted), light-gray metal panel and dark-gray metallic metal panel bands above/below the glazing, aluminium vertical mullion fins (CDR photo keys 1-4)
items.note: CDR p.9 photos (reference only)

items.name: Roof (tapered fascia) edge height above apron, north part (t -350..-310)
items.method: h = (band20 + band24 - p) / ((s20 - s24) . n) (dom_heights.py; |s20| calibrated 1.19 +- 0.03)
items.note: fascia edge and roof texture shift alike (2.2 / 2.5 m) -> one roof level at the edge; values from the s-profiles recorded in dom_heights.py

items.name: Gates
items.unit: gates (F5-F22 today; F1-F4 being rebuilt by T3W)

items.name: BA-F rotunda
items.value: octagonal rotunda hub where the arms meet (CDR massing, NAIP)

items.name: Roof height above apron, north-east arm
items.method: h = (band20 + band24 - p) / ((s20 - s24) . n) (dom_heights.py; |s20| calibrated 1.19 +- 0.03)
items.note: control against FAA DOF 06-035331 (34 ft)

items.name: FAA DOF building points on BA-F
items.note: 06-035331 (-1027.2, -211.2) roof of the NE arm; 06-035332 (-1022.1, -243.8) 16 ft at the arm tip (lower end structure or bridge rotunda)
